learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will be able to identify, construct, and seamlessly integrate Noun, Adverb, and Relative clauses to form complex, nuanced sentences.]
warm_up_hook: 🧱 Think of simple sentences as basic LEGO bricks. Clauses are the specialized connector pieces that let you build massive, intricate structures out of those basic bricks! Let's level up your sentence-building! 🏗️

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Noun Clause functions exactly like a noun. It can be a subject, an object, or an object of a preposition. They usually start with words like that, how, what, who, or whether.
examples_or_templates: Subject: What she said surprised everyone.
Object: I don't know why he left so early.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Adverb Clauses act like adverbs. They answer questions like when, where, why, how, or under what condition an action happens. They start with subordinating conjunctions (because, if, although, when, where).
examples_or_templates: Condition: If it rains, the match will be cancelled.
Concession: Although he was tired, he kept running.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Relative Clauses modify nouns or pronouns. They are introduced by relative pronouns (who, whom, whose, which, that). Defining clauses give essential information, while Non-defining clauses give extra, comma-separated information.
examples_or_templates: Defining: The book that I borrowed is lost. (Tells us exactly which book)
Non-defining: My brother, who lives in London, is visiting us. (Extra information)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the type of clause in uppercase: 'I will go WHEREVER YOU LEAD ME.'
❓ Which sentence contains a Noun Clause?
options: The girl who won the race is my sister.
I will wait until the sun goes down.
She promised that she would help me.
The house where I was born is now a museum.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: She promised that she would help me.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Combine these two sentences using a Relative Clause: 'The car is parked outside. It belongs to the principal.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use 'which' or 'that' to replace 'It' and place the clause right after 'The car'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the Noun Clause and state whether it is acting as a subject or an object: 'Whoever finishes first will get a prize.'
subjective_practice.hint: Ask yourself: Who or what is performing the action 'will get'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Complete the sentence by adding an Adverb Clause of condition: 'You will not pass the exam ____________.'

activity_or_assignment.title: 📰 The Clause Surgeon
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Take a short editorial from today's newspaper. 'Dissect' it by highlighting one Noun clause in blue, one Adverb clause in green, and one Relative clause in yellow. Write down what question each clause answers (e.g., 'who?', 'when?', 'what?').

chapter_summary: ⭐ Noun Clauses act as the subject or object of a sentence (e.g., 'I know *that you are right*').
⭐ Adverb Clauses tell us the time, reason, or condition of the main action (e.g., '*Because it rained*, we stayed indoors').
⭐ Relative Clauses act as adjectives to describe nouns, using who, which, or that.
